process.title: A controlled process from case to capital.
process.body: Every matter is case-specific. The workflow below describes the intended coordination model.

steps.title: Submit the opportunity
steps.desc: Claimant or counsel submits initial non-confidential claim overview.

steps.title: Verify claimant & authority
steps.desc: Identity verification, corporate standing, KYC/AML and conflict screening.

steps.title: Review legal merit & evidence
steps.desc: Independent legal review of cause of action, evidence burden and defenses.

steps.title: Assess budget, duration & collectability
steps.desc: Damages calculation, litigation cost budget, defendant asset & solvency audit.

steps.title: Prepare investment materials & VDR
steps.desc: Structure funder executive summary and populate secure data room.

steps.title: Present to suitable funding participants
steps.desc: Controlled, permissioned disclosure to eligible litigation capital providers.

steps.title: Structure and close vehicle
steps.desc: Negotiate funding terms, governance rights, adverse cost & security agreements.

steps.title: Monitor budgets & reporting
steps.desc: Track case milestones, legal expenditure drawdowns and procedural updates.

steps.title: Support settlement & distributions
steps.desc: Enforcement management, recovery collection and waterfall distribution.

data.title: Structuring Litigation Claims for Institutional Capital
data.excerpt: How comprehensive pre-funding diligence and structured evidence organization accelerate capital commitment in commercial disputes.

children.text: The Challenge of Raw Legal Merit

Legal merit alone is rarely sufficient for institutional litigation funders to deploy capital. Investors require clear evidence organization, realistic litigation cost budgets, supported damages calculations, and defendant collectability assessments.
By standardizing pre-funding diligence into a coherent funding dossier, claimants and law firms can significantly shorten review timelines and improve capital access terms.

data.title: Cross-Border Asset Recovery & Enforcement Analytics
data.excerpt: Evaluating defendant solvency, sovereign immunity risks, and international asset trace paths before committing litigation capital.

children.text: Enforcement as the Primary Risk Factor
Winning a tribunal award or court judgment is only the first step. Without realistic enforcement paths and verified defendant asset locations across jurisdictions, recovery remains theoretical.
Incorporating financial-crime intelligence, corporate intelligence, and asset tracing early in the dispute lifecycle ensures funding decisions are anchored in realistic recovery potential.
